issue.title: sase-core sidecar_publication classify_push_failure treats a '[remote rejected] ... cannot lock ref' push race as unknown_failure
issue.description: Rust-core push-race classifier gap: the shared classifier does not recognize the server-side ref-lock race form, so launch-time sidecar publication does not integrate and retry.

task_type_fields.impact:
Launch-time sidecar publication driven by the Rust core policy fails outright on a lost
server-side ref-lock race instead of integrating and retrying within its attempt budget.
Under multi-agent load (several agents pushing sidecar repos within seconds of each other)
this is the same transient failure that failed sase-17p.5.

Remediation: add the `[remote rejected]` + (`cannot lock ref` | `incorrect old value
provided`) match to `classify_push_failure` in
`crates/sase_core/src/sidecar_publication` with a unit test (plus a negative case for a
hook decline), then move the Python push-race classification onto the core binding. The
Python helper `is_retryable_push_race` (`src/sase/sdd/_push_race.py`) should eventually be
absorbed by the core classifier and deleted. Per the Rust core boundary this needs the
sase-core change, binding update, and a `sase-core-revision.txt` pin bump in sase.
task_type_fields.repro:
Feed `classify_push_failure` (via `decide_sidecar_publication_after_push`) the exact push
output that GitHub returned when a concurrent push moved the ref between advertisement and
update:

    ! [remote rejected] main -> main (cannot lock ref 'refs/heads/main': is at bd35e42 but expected b4b58c9)
    error: failed to push some refs to 'github.com:sase-org/sase--beads.git'

It only recognizes `non-fast-forward`, `fetch first`, and `updates were rejected because
the remote contains work`, so this output is classified `unknown_failure` (not retryable)
instead of integrate-and-retry. The same output with `incorrect old value provided` in
place of `cannot lock ref` is the other server-side phrasing. Non-race `[remote rejected]`
forms (pre-receive hook declined, protected branch, permission denied) must stay fatal, so
the marker match must be `[remote rejected]` together with one of the two race phrasings,
never `[remote rejected]` alone.

Found while fixing the sase-17p.5 commit-finalizer failure (plan
`202609/commit_finalizer_push_race_recovery.md`), where the same gap in the Python bead
sync worker classifier (`_is_non_fast_forward_rejection` in
`src/sase/bead/sync_worker.py`) turned a benign bead-store push race into a failed agent.
That change fixed the Python classifiers in place with one shared helper,
`is_retryable_push_race` in `src/sase/sdd/_push_race.py`, used by the bead sync worker and
by `is_agents_non_fast_forward` in `src/sase/agents_sync/git_sync_ops.py`.
